text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- In the government's statement to parliament, Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri pledges that citizens will not be burdened any more during the new year, says Egypt is now ready to boom after 15 years of grand achievements by President Mubarak. Government is seeking to win the people's trust. We are open to suggestions.

- The new five-year plan will provide three million job opportunities. Investments in the past 15 years amount to 373 billion pounds ($109.7 billion). Cash reserves are 19 billion pounds. Projects in Sinai, southern Egypt and the New Valley are aimed at developing 25 percent of Egypt's land.
- President Arafat and Prime Minister Netanyahu will meet today to sign a deal on redeployment in Hebron.
- Public Enterprise Minister Atef Obeid tells Saudi businessmen that there are no barriers to investing in Egypt.
- No new burdens or taxes or tariffs for the 1996/97 financial year. Mubarak will lead Egypt to safety.
- The government will raise growth rates to seven percent, lower unemployment to five percent.
- Netanyahu calls Mubarak, the president welcomes a final solution to the problem.
- Cairo will seek offers to build the city's first teleferique or aerial cable car next month.
- Netanyahu calls Mubarak to tell him about progress in the Hebron negotiations.
- Ganzouri to visit the Sheikh Zayed canal today. The 56 km canal links Abu Simbel and Toshka in southern Egypt.
